plain: Seeming reasonable or likely, though not proven

webster.text: That may be applauded; that may gain favor or approbation; hence, superficially pleasing; apparently right; specious; popular; as a plausible argument; a plausible pretext; a plausible doctrine.

more.text: Using specious arguments or discourse; as a plausible man.

example.quote: It is shifted from one to another with so much dexterity, and under such plausible appearances, that the public opinion is left in suspense about the real author.
